title: Ressource-oriented case management to implement recommendations for patients with chronic pain and frequent use of analgesics in general practices - cluster-randomised controlled trial
summary:
Chronic pain that is not caused by cancer is a very common reason for consultation in primary care practices. Experts agree that pain is influenced by physical, psychological, and social factors. Therefore, self-care—that is, things patients can do themselves, apart from taking medication, to relieve their pain—is very important. This includes, for example, knowledge about pain, physical activity, and psychological approaches. Physicians and therapists often need a great deal of information in order to recommend a treatment that fits the individual person as well as possible. For general practitioners, it can be challenging to offer such holistic pain management in their practices.

Within the RELIEF project, a care program was developed to support general practitioners in implementing key guideline recommendations for pain management. The program has five main components: (1) a computer-based pain questionnaire, (2) informational materials for patients, (3) an online training course for general practitioners and medical assistants, (4) structured appointments in the general practice, and (5) a collection of materials with helpful resources for pain treatment. The care program has already been tested and refined in a pilot study in six primary care practices.

The aim of the present study is to examine, in a larger trial, whether the program leads to improvements in pain and in the quality of care. For this purpose, 28 practices and 252 patients in Baden-Württemberg are to be recruited to voluntarily implement the program over the course of one year. To identify patients who meet all necessary eligibility criteria for participation, a screening questionnaire will be distributed to 150 adult individuals in each practice. Patients are eligible to participate if they have experienced chronic non-cancer pain for more than three months, if this pain causes at least moderate impairment in at least two areas of life, if they have taken analgesics as a result of this pain within the past four months, and if they are able to actively participate in the study. Before the start and at the end of the program, all participants will be asked to complete a questionnaire. In addition, all participants will be invited to share their personal experiences with the program in an interview.

interventions.name: Case management program with the following key components: software-based pain assessment; five structured consultation appointments; e-learning on chronic non-cancer pain for general practitioners and medical practice assistants; educational materials for patients; compilation of materials.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Chronic non-cancer pain for at least 3 months
Use of analgesic medication due to chronic pain within the past 4 weeks
At least moderate pain-related impairment in at least two areas of life
Ability to actively participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Palliative care situation
cancer-related pain
